- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing mean reversion in the middle of the forecast window.
- After a price spike (e.g., 76+), model often overshoots and fails to correct downward, underestimating subsequent decline.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — model takes longer to adjust downward than actual price does.
- When history includes recent low prices, model fails to recognize the trend and overcorrects upward.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of mean reversion after sharp spikes — fails to anticipate how quickly prices return to prior levels.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the long term (15–30 days) — exhibits asymmetric bias.
- Model does not adequately account for volatility clustering — overestimates calm periods and underestimates sudden drops.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast above 70 for several days.
